target_customer: At YC: D2C e-commerce brands and content creators; now brands and agencies in Latin America running influencer and UGC campaigns
problem: Brands find, contact, contract and pay creators across scattered tools and agencies charging 25 to 40 percent; Lizza consolidates the workflow, first as an AI assistant and now as an all-in-one platform.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for influencer and UGC campaign management (pricing not found)

founders.name: Julian May
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page, which gives no background.

competitors.name: GRIN
competitors.what: Creator management platform for direct-to-consumer brands; named on Lizza's own site as a tool it replaces
competitors.traction_then: Revenue tripled year over year per the October 2021 announcement
competitors.funding_then: $110M Series B in October 2021 at a $910M valuation, after a $26M Series A in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Creator search, outreach automation and contracts are mostly integration and workflow software; the AI assistant layer used off-the-shelf models.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded influencer platforms existed, and the site itself positions Lizza against Grin, Upfluence and Modash; local focus on Latin America is the main differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; Lizza is still listed as active and now targets Latin America.

market_need_then: D2C brands relied on influencer marketing and agencies took 25 to 40 percent fees per Lizza's own site; GRIN's 2021 raise at a $910M valuation showed investor demand for the category.

branding.domain_note: Uses lizza.link, a .link domain, not an exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, Spanish-language, cost-focused messaging about replacing many tools

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself found; search results for the name returned unrelated results.

pivots.from: AI assistant for finding and managing creator partnerships for D2C e-commerce brands (YC description)
pivots.to: All-in-one influencer marketing and UGC platform for Latin America (current site)

outcome_analysis: Lizza is listed as active with a team of seven and now claims over 1,000 brands, 20,000 creators and 40,000 collaborations in Latin America on its own site. It narrowed from a general AI assistant to a regional all-in-one platform. No verified funding or independent traction data was found, so the outcome is unclear.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists $500K total with a convertible note and Y Combinator, Speedinvest, Liquid 2 Ventures as investors; Seedtable lists a February 2022 date with no amount; none recorded. A Speedinvest portfolio page named Lizza describes a social commerce operating system, which may be a different company, so it was not used. Founding year unknown: YC page data and search summaries conflict (2024 vs batch Winter 2022), and Heidelberg appears in the directory but not in sources opened. Site claims are self-reported. Upfluence and Modash are named on the company site but no dated source for them was found. Completeness pass: the $500K convertible note rests on a single database (CB Insights, no date); Seedtable gives a 2022-02-16 date with no amount and that date is not attached to this round.
